rows.scope: Annex I 3.6.13 'Infant formulae, follow-on formulae, food for special medical purposes intended for infants and young children (3) and young-child formulae (4)' -> 3.6.13.3 'placed on the market as liquid'
rows.basis: 'The maximum level applies to the product as placed on the market.' (3.6.13 remark)
rows.evidence: '3.6.13.3 placed on the market as liquid 0,10' - Annex I pt 3.6.13.3, consolidated p.59; OJ 2024/1987 p.6/7
rows.primary_source_used: raw/regulatory/eu/eu-2023-915-consolidated-2025-10-08.pdf (02023R0915 EN 08.10.2025 006.001; EUR-Lex ALL page confirms 'In force ... Current consolidated version: 08/10/2025') + authentic OJ text http://publications.europa.eu/resource/oj/L_202401987.ENG.pdfa2a.L_202401987EN.pdf (OJ L 2024/1987, 31.7.2024)
rows.note: 0,10 mg/kg x 1000 = 100 ug/kg. Applicable from 1 July 2025 per Art 10(1)(o) inserted by Reg 2024/1987 Art 1(1)(b) ('1 July 2025 as regards the maximum levels for nickel set out in the entry 3.6 ... with the exception of ... 3.6.11.1 to 3.6.11.5'); register note 'Applies from 2025-07-01' agrees. The liquid row has no soy/non-soy split (the 0,25/0,40 split exists only for powder, 3.6.13.1/3.6.13.2), so soy_class 'both' is consistent. No later amendment to entry 3.6 appears in the 08.10.2025 consolidation (M9 = 2024/1987, M10 = 2025/1891 arsenic only).

rows.scope: Annex I 3.6.11 'Cereals' -> 3.6.11.3 'Husked rice' (sibling 3.6.11.2 'Durum wheat (Triticum durum) and rice except products listed in 3.6.11.3' = 1,5 mg/kg)
rows.basis: No row-specific basis remark; Article 2(3) general rule: 'shall apply to food as placed on the market and to the edible part of the food concerned'. 3.6.11 remark excludes cereals used for beer/distillates whose residue is not placed on the market as food.
rows.evidence: '3.6.11.3 Husked rice 2,0 As from 1 July 2026' - Annex I pt 3.6.11.3, consolidated p.58-59; OJ p.6/7
rows.primary_source_used: raw/regulatory/eu/eu-2023-915-consolidated-2025-10-08.pdf (02023R0915 EN 08.10.2025 006.001; EUR-Lex ALL page confirms 'In force ... Current consolidated version: 08/10/2025') + authentic OJ text http://publications.europa.eu/resource/oj/L_202401987.ENG.pdfa2a.L_202401987EN.pdf (OJ L 2024/1987, 31.7.2024)
rows.note: 2,0 mg/kg x 1000 = 2000 ug/kg. Applicable from 1 July 2026 per Art 10(1)(p) ('1 July 2026 as regards the maximum levels for nickel set out in points 3.6.11.1 to 3.6.11.5'); as of 2026-09-02 the level is applicable. Register note 'Applies from 2026-07-01' agrees. Register basis 'product as placed on market' is supported by Art 2(3) since the Annex row states nothing else.

rows.scope: Annex I 3.6.8 'Seaweed' -> 3.6.8.1 'Seaweed except products listed in 3.6.8.2' (3.6.8.2 'Wakame' = 40 mg/kg)
rows.basis: 'For dry seaweed the maximum level applies to the product as placed on the market. For fresh seaweed the maximum level applies after washing and separating the edible part. For fresh seaweed the maximum level applies on a dry matter basis (1)' (footnote 1: dry matter per Reg (EC) No 333/2007)
rows.evidence: '3.6.8.1 Seaweed except products listed in 3.6.8.2 30' - Annex I pt 3.6.8.1, consolidated p.57; OJ p.5/7
rows.primary_source_used: raw/regulatory/eu/eu-2023-915-consolidated-2025-10-08.pdf (02023R0915 EN 08.10.2025 006.001; EUR-Lex ALL page confirms 'In force ... Current consolidated version: 08/10/2025') + authentic OJ text http://publications.europa.eu/resource/oj/L_202401987.ENG.pdfa2a.L_202401987EN.pdf (OJ L 2024/1987, 31.7.2024)
rows.note: 30 mg/kg x 1000 = 30000 ug/kg. Applicable from 1 July 2025 per Art 10(1)(o); register note agrees. Register basis 'product as placed on market' is the instrument's basis for DRY seaweed; for FRESH seaweed the instrument applies the same number on a dry-matter basis after washing/separating the edible part - a simplification in the register wording, not a numeric or scope conflict. Register scope 'seaweed except wakame' mirrors 3.6.8.1 exactly.

rows.scope: Tenth Schedule (Regulation 31(1)) 'MAXIMUM AMOUNTS OF ARSENIC AND LEAD PERMITTED IN FOOD', (b) Other Food - (2) 'Canned fish and meat, meat extract and hydrolysed protein', Arsenic (As) column, parts per million
rows.basis: Reg 31(1): 'No person shall import, sell, advertise, manufacture, consign or deliver any article of food containing arsenic and lead in amounts in excess of those specified in the Tenth Schedule' - i.e. the food as imported/sold; no separate basis stated for this row (only row (20) infant formula carries 'as consumed').
rows.evidence: '(2) Canned fish and meat, meat extract and hydrolysed protein 1 2' - Tenth Schedule (b)(2), 2005 Ed. p.211
rows.primary_source_used: raw/regulatory/sg/singapore-food-regulations-heavy-metals-2026.pdf (SSO informal consolidation 'version in force from 30/1/2026') + https://sso.agc.gov.sg/SL/SFA1973-RG1?ProvIds=Sc10- (SSO 'Current version as at 02 Sep 2026')
rows.note: 1 ppm x 1000 = 1000 ug/kg. Held PDF text and live SSO Tenth Schedule (current version as at 02 Sep 2026) are identical for this row; Schedule last amended S 59/2019 wef 01/02/2019. 'Arsenic (As)' is unspeciated total arsenic (inorganic-arsenic limits exist separately only for seaweed 2 ppm, polished rice 0.2 ppm, husked rice 0.35 ppm under reg 31(2)-(2B)), consistent with metal_species tAs. Note the packet's register_urls/url are empty; SSO id is SFA1973-RG1 (the -R1 form returns Page Not Found).

rows.scope: Tenth Schedule (Regulation 31(1)), (b) Other Food - (15) 'Fish, crustaceans and molluscs', Arsenic (As) column, parts per million
rows.basis: Reg 31(1): food as imported/sold ('import, sell, advertise, manufacture, consign or deliver any article of food containing arsenic ... in excess of those specified in the Tenth Schedule'); no separate basis stated for this row.
rows.evidence: '(15) Fish, crustaceans and molluscs 1 2' - Tenth Schedule (b)(15), 2005 Ed. p.212
rows.primary_source_used: raw/regulatory/sg/singapore-food-regulations-heavy-metals-2026.pdf (SSO informal consolidation 'version in force from 30/1/2026') + https://sso.agc.gov.sg/SL/SFA1973-RG1?ProvIds=Sc10- (SSO 'Current version as at 02 Sep 2026')
rows.note: 1 ppm x 1000 = 1000 ug/kg. Identical in held PDF (version in force from 30/1/2026) and live SSO (current version as at 02 Sep 2026). Total (unspeciated) arsenic, consistent with tAs. Register 'as sold or imported' basis matches reg 31(1).

rows.scope: (as restated by ANSES) 'Valeurs maximales en elements traces et en iode dans les algues legumes ou condiments recommandees par le CSHPF' - algae consumed as vegetables or condiments, human food
rows.basis: (as restated) 'en mg.kg-1 de matiere seche (MS)' / 'poids sec' - dry weight
rows.successor: CANDIDATE, not confirmed adopted: Avis Anses 2017-SA-0070 (21 July 2020) identifies Cd 0,35 mg/kg dry matter (CI 0.18-1.09) and recommends a level 'aussi basse que possible'; CEVA 2024 (updated 7/01/2025) still lists CSHPF Cd 0,5 as the French criterion
rows.evidence: 'Cadmium 0,5' - Anses avis 2017-SA-0070 Tableau 3 (CSHPF, mg.kg-1 MS), p.10/61
rows.primary_source_used: PRIMARY NOT LOCATED. Secondary official restatement: https://www.anses.fr/fr/system/files/ERCA2017SA0070.pdf (Avis Anses 2017-SA-0070, 21 juillet 2020, Tableau 3 p.10/61); industry compilation https://www.ceva-algues.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/10/V14-synthese-reglementaire2024-1.pdf (Synthese CEVA 2024, MAJ 7/01/2025, Tableau 3)
rows.note: Primary instrument (avis CSHPF, seances 14 juin 1988, 13 decembre 1988, 9 janvier 1990) is unreachable: raw/regulatory/fr/ does not exist in the repo, no held copy anywhere under raw/, row has no URL, and per CEVA the avis was 'non paru au Journal Officiel'. DGCCRF pages/PDFs (economie.gouv.fr) return 403 to fetchers and the reachable DGCCRF contaminants page contains no seaweed passage. Two independent restatements (ANSES 2020 official avis; CEVA 2024 compilation) both give Cd 0,5 mg/kg dry matter = 500 ug/kg, equal to the register value, and both give the companion set iAs 3 / Hg 0,1 / Pb 5 / Sn 5 mg/kg MS, iodine 2000 - so the register row is corroborated but not verified against the instrument text. Status: a non-binding CSHPF recommendation (ANSES calls it 'particulierement ancienne (1990)') that DGCCRF still used as its management reference at the 2020 saisine; whether DGCCRF later adopted the ANSES 0,35 value could not be established. Register basis 'dry weight' and status 'recommended maximum level' are consistent with the restatements.

rows.scope: (as restated by ANSES) 'algues legumes ou condiments' - algae consumed as vegetables or condiments, human food
rows.basis: (as restated) 'en mg.kg-1 de matiere seche (MS)' - dry weight
rows.evidence: 'Mercure 0,1' - Anses avis 2017-SA-0070 Tableau 3 (CSHPF, mg.kg-1 MS), p.10/61
rows.primary_source_used: PRIMARY NOT LOCATED. Secondary official restatement: https://www.anses.fr/fr/system/files/ERCA2017SA0070.pdf (Avis Anses 2017-SA-0070, 21 juillet 2020, Tableau 3 p.10/61); industry compilation https://www.ceva-algues.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/10/V14-synthese-reglementaire2024-1.pdf (Synthese CEVA 2024, MAJ 7/01/2025, Tableau 3)
rows.note: Same unreachable primary as fr_cshpf_seaweed_cd_500 (CSHPF avis never published in the JO; no raw/regulatory/fr/ directory; no URL). ANSES 2020 Tableau 3 and CEVA 2024 Tableau 3 both restate 'Mercure 0,1' mg/kg dry matter = 100 ug/kg, equal to the register value; 'Mercure' is unspeciated total mercury, consistent with tHg. ANSES 2020 found 'tres peu de depassements' of the CSHPF values for mercury and proposed no replacement value, so no successor is identified. Register value corroborated by secondary official restatement but not verified against the instrument text.
